jobs.description: The German Diabetes Center (DDZ), Leibniz Institute for Diabetes Research at the Heinrich Heine University (HHU) Düsseldorf is an interdisciplinary research institute that links basic and clinical sciences to improve prevention, diagnosis and therapy of Diabetes mellitus and its complications. The Junior Research Group Crosstalk (head: Dr. Melanie Mittenbühler) at the Institute for Clinical Biochemistry and Pathobiochemistry focuses on how inter-tissue communication impacts energy balance and metabolic health. We are seeking a talented and highly motivatedPostdoctoral Fellow (PhD/Dr. rer. nat., m/f/div., E13 TV-L 100%) to join our research group. Our group investigates how skeletal muscle acts as an endocrine organ and communicates with other tissues through secreted signaling molecules, particularly myokines. In the ERC Starting Grant project MYOSCAN, we systematically investigate how exercise and age-related muscle loss alter the skeletal muscle secretome. We aim to identify novel exercise-sensitive myokines and define their roles in sarcopenia, metabolic disease, and cancer biology. A central question is whether muscle-derived factors promote or suppress tumor growth and how these signaling pathways can be therapeutically targeted.PhD in molecular biology, cell biology, biochemistry, physiology, exercise science, metabolism, cancer biology, or a related fieldStrong expertise in at least one of the following areas: proteomics/mass spectrometry, secretome analysis, cell biology, molecular signaling, metabolic research, or cancer biology. Experience in working with mouse models is preferredScientific curiosity, initiative, strong analytical skills, and the ability to work both independently and collaborativelyExcellent written and spoken English skillsExperience in supervising students or doctoral researchersWe provide a fully funded postdoctoral position within an excellently supported ERC Starting Grant project, an exciting, dynamic and international working environment, and a structured and coherent mentoring and training program. You will be able to learn state-of-the-art methodologies in a team of young scientists. Initially, the position is to be awarded for 2 years starting from 01.03.2027 or later. An extension of the contract period is envisaged. The employment contract is governed by TV-L in its current version for North Rhine-Westphalia, including the special regulations regarding the scientific area. The salary is based on qualification and experience, according to TV-L.Females are especially encouraged to apply, and in the case of equal qualification, handicapped persons will be given preference. jobs.occupation: Research Associate (PhD position) for the DFG project (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: Ihre AufgabenThe University of Bonn is an international research university offering a broad range of subjects. With a 200-year history, some 31,500 students, more than 6,000 employees and an outstanding reputation in Germany and abroad, the University of Bonn is one of the leading universities in Germany and has been awarded the status of a University of Excellence.The Department of Southeastasia is looking to fill the following position from January 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible, initially on a fixed-term contract according to § 2(1) WissZeitVG until December, 31, 2029Research Associate (PhD position) for the DFG project (65%)Working the Plantationocene. Ecological Labour Regimes of the Palm Oil Value Chain (PALMWORK)PALMWORK examines the relationship between labour and the environment along the palm oil value chain, particularly in the areas of production (plantations and oil mills) and social reproduction. The project is designed as a qualitative comparative analysis of case studies from Northeast India, Ghana and Colombia. It builds on re-search from the fields of labour regime analysis, (feminist) labour geography, environmental labour studies and political ecology on the materiality of nature and the society–nature metabolism. The project is being carried out as part of the DFG Priority Programme 2575 'Sustainability and Resilience of Agri-Food Chains' and consists of three sub-projects located at the University of Bonn, the Free University of Berlin and the University of Kassel. The position is for the sub-project in Northeast India, and is based at Bonn University.Tasks:- Field research with plantation and mill workers in North-East India- Contribution to joint publications- Contribution to science communicationProfile:- A completed academic degree (Master's) in the social sciences or earth sci-ences (political science, human geography, regional studies, sociology or equivalent)- Willingness to conduct independent field research in Northeast India- Very good spoken and written English- Good communication and teamwork skills- Intercultural and diversity competenceDesirable:- Experience of conducting independent research in India- Good knowledge of qualitative research methods- Experience with working and researching with (palm oil) workers- Good command of a language spoken in Northeast India (e.g. Assamese, Bengali, Nepali)- Good knowledge of the project's research area (political ecology, political economy, analysis of labour regimes, environmental labour studies, labour ge ography)What we offer:- Opportunity to pursue a PhD- Be part of a cutting-edge research team- Be part of a larger network of scholars in the DFG Special Programme- Flexible working hours and the ability to work from home- Remuneration in accordance with TV-L pay grade 13The University of Bonn promotes an open, respectful, and non-discriminatory academic culture and is actively committed to equal opportunity and family friendliness. We aim to eliminate structural disadvantages and to strengthen diversity in research, teaching, and administration. Therefore, we welcome all applications, regard-less of ethnic or social background, gender, sexual orientation, religion or belief, disability, or age.Applications from women and people with a documented severe disability (or equivalent status) will be given preferential consideration in accordance with the State Equality Act (LGG) NRW and Social Code (SGB) IXProject start is January 1st, 2027. Please send your application (with motivation letter, CV and writing sample (if available) with the application code 2026/447 to opye@uni-bonn.de. Application deadline is 22th November, 2026.
